cues.en: People at the back, can you hear me clearly?
cues.zh: 后排的朋友，能听清我说话吗？

cues.en: Okay. Good.
cues.zh: 好，很好。

cues.en: Have you ever
cues.zh: 你有没有过

cues.en: held a question in mind
cues.zh: 把一个问题一直放在心上

cues.en: for so long
cues.zh: 想了很久

cues.en: that it becomes
cues.zh: 以至于它成了

cues.en: part of how you think?
cues.zh: 你思考方式的一部分？

cues.en: Maybe even part of who you are as a person?
cues.zh: 甚至成了你这个人的一部分？

cues.en: Well, I've had a question in my mind for many, many years, and that is,
cues.zh: 嗯，有一个问题在我心里盘桓了很多很多年，那就是，

cues.en: how can you speed up learning?
cues.zh: 怎样才能加快学习速度？

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: this is an interesting question because if you speed up learning, you can spend less time at school.
cues.zh: 这是个有趣的问题，因为如果你加快学习，就能少花点时间待在学校。

cues.en: And if you learn really fast,
cues.zh: 而如果你学得真的很快，

cues.en: you probably wouldn't have to go to school at all.
cues.zh: 你可能根本就不用上学了。

cues.en: Now, when I was young,
cues.zh: 那么，我小时候，

cues.en: school was sort of okay, but I
cues.zh: 学校还算凑合，但我

cues.en: found quite often that school got in the way of learning.
cues.zh: 常常发现学校反而妨碍了学习。

cues.en: So I had this question in mind, how do you learn faster?
cues.zh: 所以我心里一直有这个问题：怎样才能学得更快？

cues.en: And this began when I was very, very young. When I was 11 years old, I wrote a letter to researchers in The Soviet Union asking about hypnopedia.
cues.zh: 这要从我很小很小的时候说起。11岁那年，我给苏联的研究人员写了一封信，询问睡眠学习法。

cues.en: This is sleep learning, where you get a tape recorder, you put it beside your bed, and it turns on in the middle of the night when you're sleeping,
cues.zh: 这就是睡眠学习：你拿一台录音机，放在床边，它会在半夜你睡觉时打开，

cues.en: and you're supposed to be learning from this.
cues.zh: 而你本应通过它来学习。

cues.en: Good idea. Unfortunately, it doesn't work. But, hypnopedia
cues.zh: 想法不错。可惜行不通。不过，睡眠学习法

cues.en: did open the doors to research in other areas, and we've had incredible discoveries about learning that began with that first question.
cues.zh: 确实为其他领域的研究打开了大门，而我们关于学习的那些惊人发现，正是始于那个最初的问题。

cues.en: I went on from there to become passionate about psychology,
cues.zh: 从那以后，我开始对心理学充满热情，

cues.en: and I have been involved in psychology in many different ways for the rest of my life up until this point.
cues.zh: 而在此后的人生中，直到现在，我一直以各种不同方式参与心理学。

cues.en: I took myself to China,
cues.zh: 我去了中国，

cues.en: and I decided that I was going to be native level in Chinese inside two years.
cues.zh: 我决定要在两年内把中文达到母语水平。

cues.en: Now, you need to understand
cues.zh: 现在，你需要明白

cues.en: that in 1981,
everybody thought Chinese was really, really difficult,
cues.zh: 所有人都认为中文非常非常难，

cues.en: and that a westerner could study for ten years or more and never really get very good at it.
cues.zh: 西方人可能学十年甚至更久，也学不好。

cues.en: And I also went in with a different idea which was taking all of the conclusions from psychological research up to that point and applying them to the learning process.
cues.zh: 我还带着一个不同的想法：把当时心理学研究的所有结论，应用到学习过程中。

cues.en: What was really cool was that in six months I was fluent in Mandarin Chinese, and it took a little bit longer to get up to native.
cues.zh: 很酷的是，六个月后我就能说流利的普通话了，达到母语水平则多花了一点时间。

cues.en: But I looked around and I saw all of these people
cues.zh: 但我环顾四周，看到所有这些

cues.en: from different countries struggling terribly with Chinese. I saw Chinese people struggling terribly
cues.zh: 来自不同国家的人都在中文上苦苦挣扎。我看到中国人在

cues.en: to learn English in other languages.
cues.zh: 学英语和其他语言时也苦苦挣扎。

cues.en: And so,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: my question got refined
cues.zh: 我的问题逐渐明确，

cues.en: down to how can you help a normal adult
cues.zh: 归结为：如何帮助一个普通成年人

cues.en: learn a new language quickly, easily, and effectively?
cues.zh: 快速、轻松、有效地学会一门新语言？

cues.en: Now, this is a really, really important question in today's world. We have massive challenges with environment. We have massive challenges with social dislocation,
cues.zh: 在当今世界，这是一个非常非常重要的问题。我们在环境方面面临巨大挑战。我们在社会失序方面面临巨大挑战，

cues.en: with wars. All sorts of things going on, and if we can't communicate,
cues.zh: 还有战争。各种事情层出不穷，如果我们无法沟通，

cues.en: we're really gonna have difficulty solving these problems. So we need to be able to speak each other's languages. This is really really important.
cues.zh: 就很难解决这些问题。所以我们需要能够说彼此的语言。这真的真的非常重要。

cues.en: The question is how do you do that?
cues.zh: 问题是怎么做到这一点？

cues.en: Well, it's actually really easy.
cues.zh: 其实非常简单。

cues.en: You look around for people who can already do it,
cues.zh: 看看周围那些已经做得到的人，

cues.en: you look for situations where it's already working,
cues.zh: 找找那些已经行之有效的案例，

cues.en: and then you identify the principles and apply them. It's called modeling, and I've been looking at language learning and modeling language learning for about fifteen to twenty years now.
cues.zh: 然后提炼出背后的原则并加以运用。这叫做“建模”，过去十五到二十年里，我一直在研究语言学习并对其进行建模。

cues.en: And my conclusion, my observation from this is that any adult can learn a second language to fluency inside six months.
cues.zh: 由此我得出的观察和结论是：任何成年人都能在六个月内流利掌握一门外语。

cues.en: Now when I say this,
cues.zh: 每当我这么说，

cues.en: most people think I'm crazy. This is not possible.
cues.zh: 大多数人都觉得我疯了，认为这绝不可能。

cues.en: So let me remind everybody
cues.zh: 那我就带大家回顾一下

cues.en: of the history of human progress. It's all about expanding our limits.
cues.zh: 人类的进步史。它本身就是一部不断突破极限的历史。

cues.en: everybody believed that running one mile in four minutes was impossible.
cues.zh: 所有人都坚信，四分钟跑完一英里是根本不可能的。

cues.en: And then Roger Bannister did it in 1956,
cues.zh: 然而 Roger Bannister 在1956年做到了，

cues.en: and from there it's got shorter and shorter.
cues.zh: 从那之后，纪录被不断刷新，用时越来越短。

cues.en: A hundred years ago, everybody believed that heavy stuff doesn't fly,
cues.zh: 一百年前，大家也都相信重物是飞不起来的，

cues.en: except it does, and we all know this.
cues.zh: 但事实证明能飞，这一点我们如今都很清楚。

cues.en: How does heavy stuff fly? We reorganize the material using principles that we have learned from observing
cues.zh: 重物是怎么飞起来的？我们运用通过观察自然

cues.en: nature, birds in this case.
cues.zh: （具体来说是观察鸟类）学到的原理，重新组合材料。

cues.en: And today,
cues.zh: 而到了今天，

cues.en: we've gone even further.
cues.zh: 我们走得更远了。

cues.en: We've
cues.zh: 我们

cues.en: gone even further. So you can fly a car.
cues.zh: 走得更远了，你甚至能开着汽车飞。

cues.en: You can buy one of these for a couple 100,000 US dollars.
cues.zh: 花上几十万美元就能买到一辆。

cues.en: We now have cars in the world that fly. And there's a different way to fly which we learn from squirrels.
cues.zh: 现在的世界上已经有了会飞的汽车。不仅如此，我们还从松鼠身上学到了另一种飞行方式。

cues.en: So all you need to do is copy what a flying squirrel does, build a suit called a wingsuit, and off you go. You can fly like a squirrel.
cues.zh: 你只要模仿飞鼠的动作，做一套叫做翼装的衣服，就能出发了。你可以像松鼠一样在空中飞翔。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: most people,
cues.zh: 大多数人，

cues.en: a lot of people, I wouldn't say everybody, but a lot of people think they can't draw.
cues.zh: 很多人——我不敢说所有人，但很多人都觉得自己不会画画。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 然而，

cues.en: there are some key principles, five principles that you can apply
cues.zh: 有几个核心原则，只要掌握这五条原则，

cues.en: for learning to draw and you can actually learn to draw in five days. So if you draw like this,
cues.zh: 用来学画画，你其实在五天之内就能学会。如果你现在画成这样，

cues.en: you learn these principles for five days and apply them, and after five days you can draw something like this.
cues.zh: 花五天时间学习并运用这些原则，五天后你就能画成这样了。

cues.en: Now I know this is true because that was my first drawing, and after five days of applying these principles, that was what I was able to do. And I looked at this and I went, wow. So that's how I look like when I'm concentrating so intensely that my brain is exploding.
cues.zh: 我知道这是真的，因为前面那是我的第一幅画，而在运用这些原则五天之后，我就能画成后面这样了。我看着这幅画心想：哇，原来我全神贯注、脑子快要爆炸的时候是长这样的。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: anybody can learn to draw in five days.
cues.zh: 任何人都可以在五天内学会画画。

cues.en: And in the same way, with the same logic, anybody can learn a second language in six months.
cues.zh: 同理，按照同样的逻辑，任何人都可以在六个月内掌握一门外语。

cues.en: How? There are five principles and seven actions.
cues.zh: 怎么做？答案是五条原则和七个行动。

cues.en: There may be a few more, but these are absolutely core.
cues.zh: 可能还有别的，但这几条绝对是最核心的。

cues.en: And before I get into those, I just want to talk about two myths. I want to dispel two myths.
cues.zh: 在展开讲之前，我想先破除两个迷思。

cues.en: The first is that you need talent. Let me tell you about Zoe.
cues.zh: 第一个迷思是“你需要有天赋”。让我给你们讲讲 Zoe 的故事。

cues.en: Zoe came from Australia, went to Holland, was trying to learn Dutch,
cues.zh: Zoe 来自澳大利亚，去了荷兰，试着学习荷兰语，

cues.en: struggling extremely,
cues.zh: 学得极其吃力，

cues.en: extremely a great deal, and finally, you know, people were saying, you're completely useless, you're you're you're not talented, give up, you're a waste of time, and she was very very depressed. And then she came across these five principles,
cues.zh: 过程非常痛苦。最后大家都在说：“你根本不行，你毫无天赋，放弃吧，完全是浪费时间。”她当时非常非常沮丧。后来，她接触到了这五条原则，

cues.en: she moved to Brazil, and she applied them, and in six months she was fluent in Portuguese. So talent doesn't matter.
cues.zh: 她搬到了巴西并加以运用，六个月后，她就能说一口流利的葡萄牙语了。所以，天赋根本不重要。

cues.en: People also think that immersion in a new country is the way to learn a language. But look around Hong Kong. Look at all the westerners who've been here for ten years, who don't speak a word of Chinese.
cues.zh: 人们还认为，沉浸在一个新国家是学习语言的方法。但看看香港。看看那些在这里待了十年，一句中文都不会说的西方人。

cues.en: Look at all the Chinese living in America, Britain, Australia, Canada, who've been there ten, twenty years, and they don't speak any English.
cues.zh: 看看那些生活在美国、英国、澳大利亚、加拿大的中国人，他们在那里待了十年、二十年，却不会说任何英语。

cues.en: Immersion
cues.zh: 沉浸式

cues.en: per se does not work. Why? Because a drowning man cannot learn to swim.
cues.zh: 本身并不奏效。为什么？因为溺水的人学不会游泳。

cues.en: When you don't speak a language, you're like a baby, and if you drop yourself into a context which is all adults talking about stuff over your head, you won't learn.
cues.zh: 当你不会说一门语言时，你就像个婴儿，如果你把自己丢进一个全是成年人谈论你听不懂的话题的环境里，你是学不会的。

cues.en: So, what are the five principles that you need to pay attention to? First,
cues.zh: 那么，你需要关注哪五个原则呢？首先，

cues.en: the four words. Attention, meaning, relevance, and memory. And these interconnect
cues.zh: 四个词。注意力、意义、相关性和记忆。它们之间有着

cues.en: in very very important ways.
cues.zh: 非常重要的相互联系。

cues.en: Especially when you're talking about learning. Come with me on a journey through a forest. You go on a walk through a forest and you see something like this. Those marks on a tree. Maybe you pay attention, maybe you don't.
cues.zh: 尤其是谈到学习的时候。跟我一起走过一片森林。你在森林里散步，看到这样的东西。树上的那些标记。也许你会注意，也许不会。

cues.en: You go another 50 meters and you see this.
cues.zh: 你再走50米，看到这个。

cues.en: You should be paying attention.
cues.zh: 你应该注意了。

cues.en: Another 50 meters, if you hadn't been paying attention, you see this. And at this point, you're paying attention.
cues.zh: 再走50米，如果你之前没注意，你会看到这个。到这时，你就会注意了。

cues.en: And you've just learned that this is important, it's relevant because it means this,
cues.zh: 你刚刚学到这是重要的，它有意义，因为它意味着这个，

cues.en: and anything
cues.zh: 而任何

cues.en: that is related, any information related to your survival
cues.zh: 相关的，任何与你的生存相关的信息

cues.en: is stuff that you're going to pay attention to and therefore you're to remember it. If it's related to your own personal goals,
cues.zh: 都是你会去注意、因此会记住的东西。如果它与你的个人目标相关，

cues.en: then you're going to pay attention to it. It's relevant. You're going to remember it. So the first rule, first principle for learning a language is focus on language content that is relevant to you. Which brings us to tools.
cues.zh: 那你就会注意它。它有相关性。你会记住它。所以学习语言的第一条规则、第一个原则就是专注于与你相关的语言内容。这就引出了工具。

cues.en: We master tools by using tools, and we learn tools the fastest
cues.zh: 我们通过使用工具来掌握工具，而掌握工具最快的时机，

cues.en: when
cues.zh: 就是当

cues.en: they're relevant to us. So let me share a story. A keyboard is a tool.
cues.zh: 它们与我们切身相关的时候。我来分享一个故事。键盘是一种工具。

cues.en: Typing Chinese a certain way, there are methods for this, that's a tool. I had a colleague many years ago
cues.zh: 用某种方式打中文——比如各种输入法，也是一种工具。很多年前我有一位同事，

cues.en: who went to night school Tuesday night, Thursday night, two hours each time practicing at home. She spent nine months and she did not learn to type Chinese.
cues.zh: 她每周二、周四晚上去上夜校，每次回家练习两小时。她花了九个月，却还是没学会中文打字。

cues.en: And one night we had a crisis.
cues.zh: 直到有一晚，我们遇到了紧急情况。

cues.en: We had forty eight hours to deliver a training manual in Chinese,
cues.zh: 我们必须在48小时内交付一份中文培训手册，

cues.en: and she got the job. And I can guarantee you, in forty eight hours, she learned to type Chinese because it was relevant, it was meaningful, it was important, she was using a tool to create value.
cues.zh: 这项任务交给了她。我敢向你保证，就在这48小时里，她学会了中文打字，因为这与她切身相关、意义重大、至关重要，她是在用工具创造价值。

cues.en: So the second principle for learning a language is to use your language as a tool to communicate right from day one,
cues.zh: 所以语言学习的第二个原则是：从第一天起，就把语言当作沟通的工具来用，

cues.en: as a kid does.
cues.zh: 就像小孩子那样。

cues.en: I first arrived in China, didn't speak a word of Chinese,
cues.zh: 我刚到中国时，一句中文都不会说，

cues.en: and on my second week I got to take a train ride overnight.
cues.zh: 到了第二周，我坐了一趟过夜火车。

cues.en: I spent eight hours sitting in the dining car talking to one of the guards on the train. He took an interest in me for some reason.
cues.zh: 我在餐车里坐了八个小时，和列车上的一名乘务员聊天。不知道为什么，他对我挺感兴趣。

cues.en: And we just chatted all night in Chinese, and he was drawing pictures and making movements with his hands and facial expressions, and piece by piece by piece I understood more and more.
cues.zh: 我们就用中文聊了一整夜，他又是画画，又是比划手势、做表情，一点一滴地，我懂的越来越多。

cues.en: But what was really cool was two weeks later,
cues.zh: 但真正神奇的是两周之后，

cues.en: when people were talking Chinese around me, I was understanding some of this and I hadn't even made any effort to learn that.
cues.zh: 当身边的人讲中文时，我竟然能听懂一部分了，而我甚至根本没有刻意去学过。

cues.en: What had happened, I'd absorbed it that night on the train, which brings us to the third principle.
cues.zh: 那天晚上在火车上，我已经全吸收了，这就引出了第三个原则。

cues.en: When you first understand the message,
cues.zh: 当你先理解了传达的信息，

cues.en: then you will acquire
cues.zh: 你就会

cues.en: the language unconsciously.
cues.zh: 不知不觉地掌握这门语言。

cues.en: And this is really, really well documented now. It's something called comprehensible input. There's twenty or thirty years of research on this. Stephen Krashen, a leader in the field has published all sorts of these different studies,
cues.zh: 如今这已经有非常充分的研究佐证。这被称为“可理解性输入”。相关研究已有二三十年。该领域的领军人物 Stephen Krashen 发表过各种相关研究，

cues.en: and this is just from one of them. The purple bars show the scores on different tests
cues.zh: 这只是其中之一。紫色柱子展示了各项语言测试

cues.en: for language.
cues.zh: 的得分。

cues.en: The purple
cues.zh: 紫色代表的

cues.en: people were people who had learned by grammar and formal study. The green ones are the ones who learned by comprehensible input.
cues.zh: 是通过语法和正规课程学习的人。绿色代表的则是通过可理解性输入学习的人。

cues.en: So comprehension
cues.zh: 所以理解

cues.en: works.
cues.zh: 是有效的。

cues.en: Comprehension is key.
cues.zh: 理解才是关键。

cues.en: And language learning is not about
cues.zh: 语言学习并不是

cues.en: accumulating
cues.zh: 去积累

cues.en: lots of knowledge.
cues.zh: 大量的知识。

cues.en: In many, many ways, it's about physiological
cues.zh: 在很大程度上，它其实是一种生理

cues.en: training.
cues.zh: 训练。

cues.en: A woman I know from Taiwan did great in English at school. She got A grades all the way through, went through college, A grades, went to The US,
cues.zh: 我认识一位台湾女士，在学校时英语非常好。一路拿 A，大学也是全 A，后来去了美国，

cues.en: and found she couldn't understand what people were saying.
cues.zh: 却发现自己根本听不懂别人在说什么。

cues.en: And people starting us... Started asking her, are you deaf?
cues.zh: 大家开始……开始问她：“你是聋子吗？”

cues.en: And she was.
cues.zh: 其实她确实是。

cues.en: English deaf.
cues.zh: “英语耳聋”。

cues.en: Because we have filters in our brain that filter in the sounds
cues.zh: 因为我们大脑中有过滤器，会接收

cues.en: that we are familiar with, and they filter out the sounds of languages that we're not.
cues.zh: 我们熟悉的声音，而过滤掉那些我们不熟悉的语言声音。

cues.en: And if you can't hear it, you won't understand it. If you can't understand it, you're not going to learn it. So you actually have to be able to hear these sounds.
cues.zh: 如果你听不到，你就理解不了；理解不了，就学不会。所以你必须先能听到这些声音。

cues.en: And there are ways to do that, but it's physiological training. Speaking
cues.zh: 有办法做到，但那是生理训练。说话

cues.en: takes muscle.
cues.zh: 需要肌肉。

cues.en: You've got 43 muscles in your face.
cues.zh: 你脸上有43块肌肉。

cues.en: You have to coordinate those in a way that you make sounds that other people will understand.
cues.zh: 你得协调这些肌肉，才能发出别人听得懂的声音。

cues.en: If you've ever done a new sport for a couple of days and you know how your body feels, hurts,
cues.zh: 如果你试过连续几天做一项新运动，就知道身体会是什么感觉、会酸痛，

cues.en: if your face is hurting, you're doing it right.
cues.zh: 如果你的脸在疼，说明你做对了。

cues.en: And the final principle is state. Psychophysiological
cues.zh: 最后一个原则是状态。心理生理

cues.en: state.
cues.zh: 状态。

cues.en: If you're sad, angry, worried, upset, you're not going to learn. Period.
cues.zh: 如果你难过、生气、担心、烦躁，你就学不进去。就这样。

cues.en: If you're happy, relaxed,
cues.zh: 如果你开心、放松，

cues.en: in an alpha brain state, curious, you're going to learn really quickly, and very specifically, you need to be tolerant of ambiguity.
cues.zh: 处于α脑状态、充满好奇，你会学得很快；而且具体来说，你必须能容忍模糊。

cues.en: If you're one of those people who needs to understand 100%
cues.zh: 如果你是那种必须100%理解

cues.en: every word you're hearing,
cues.zh: 你听到的每一个词的人，

cues.en: you will go nuts because you'll be incredibly upset all the time because you're not perfect.
cues.zh: 你会疯掉，因为你会一直特别沮丧，因为你不完美。

cues.en: If you're comfortable with getting some, not getting some,
cues.zh: 如果你能接受听懂一部分、听不懂一部分，

cues.en: just paying attention to what you do understand, you're going to be fine, you'll be relaxed, and you'll be learning quickly.
cues.zh: 只关注你确实听懂的内容，你就会没事，会放松，而且学得很快。

cues.en: So based on those five principles, what are the seven actions that you take?
cues.zh: 那么基于这五个原则，你要采取哪七个行动？

cues.en: Number one, listen a lot.
cues.zh: 第一，大量听。

cues.en: I call it brain soaking.
cues.zh: 我称之为“大脑浸泡”。

cues.en: You put yourself in a context where you're hearing tons and tons and tons of the language, It doesn't matter if you understand it or not.
cues.zh: 把自己放进一个能听到海量这门语言的环境里，听不听得懂都无所谓。

cues.en: You're listening to the rhythms, you're listening to patterns that repeat, you're listening to things that stand out. So
cues.zh: 你在听节奏，听重复的模式，听那些突出的东西。所以

cues.en: just soak your brain in this.
cues.zh: 就让大脑沉浸其中。

cues.en: The second action is you get the meaning first, even before you get the words.
cues.zh: 第二个动作是，先理解意思，甚至在掌握词语之前就理解。

cues.en: And you go, well how do I do that? I don't know the words. Well, you understand what these different postures mean.
cues.zh: 你会问，那怎么做？我还不懂词啊。其实，你明白这些不同姿态是什么意思。

cues.en: Human communication is body language in many, many ways. So much body language.
cues.zh: 人类交流在很多很多方面都是肢体语言。肢体语言占比很大。

cues.en: From body language you can understand a lot of communication,
cues.zh: 通过肢体语言，你能理解大量交流内容，

cues.en: therefore, you're understanding, you're acquiring through comprehensible input.
cues.zh: 因此，你在理解，你在通过可理解输入来习得。

cues.en: And you can also use patterns that you already know. If you're a Chinese speaker of Mandarin and Cantonese,
cues.zh: 你也可以利用已经熟悉的模式。如果你是会说普通话和粤语的中文使用者，

cues.en: and you go to Vietnam,
cues.zh: 然后你去了越南，

cues.en: you will understand 60%
cues.zh: 你能听懂60%

cues.en: of what they say to you
cues.zh: 他们对你说的内容

cues.en: in daily conversation, because Vietnamese is about 30% Mandarin, 30% Cantonese.
cues.zh: 在日常对话中，因为越南语大约30%来自普通话，30%来自粤语。

cues.en: The third action, start mixing.
cues.zh: 第三个动作，开始混合。

cues.en: You probably have never thought of this, but if you've got 10 verbs, 10 nouns, and 10 adjectives, you can say 1,000 different things.
cues.zh: 你可能从没想过，但如果你有10个动词、10个名词和10个形容词，你能说出1000种不同内容。

cues.en: Right? Language is a creative process.
cues.zh: 对吧？语言是个创造过程。

cues.en: What do babies do?
cues.zh: 婴儿会怎么做？

cues.en: Okay. Me, but, now.
cues.zh: 好。我，但是，现在。

cues.en: Okay? That's how they communicate. So start mixing. Get creative. Have fun with it. It doesn't have to be perfect. It just has to work.
cues.zh: 看到了吗？他们就是这样交流的。所以开始混合。发挥创意。享受这个过程。不必完美，只要管用。

cues.en: And you... When you're doing this, you focus on the core.
cues.zh: 而你……做这件事时，要专注核心。

cues.en: What does that mean?
cues.zh: 这是什么意思？

cues.en: Well, with every language, there's high frequency content. In English,
cues.zh: 每种语言都有高频内容。在英语中，

cues.en: 1,000 words covers
cues.zh: 1000个词能覆盖

cues.en: of anything you're ever going to say in daily communication.
cues.zh: 你日常交流中会说的任何内容。

cues.en: 3,000 words gives you 98%
cues.zh: 3000个词能让你覆盖98%

cues.en: of anything you're going to say in daily conversation.
cues.zh: 你日常对话中会说的任何内容。

cues.en: You got 3,000 words, you're speaking the language, the rest is icing on the cake.
cues.zh: 你掌握了 3,000 个词，能够用这门语言交流，其他都只是锦上添花。

cues.en: And when you're just beginning with a new language, start with your toolbox. Week number one.
cues.zh: 当你刚开始学习一门新语言时，先从工具箱入手。第一周。

cues.en: In your new language, you say things like, how do you say that? I don't understand. Repeat that please. What does that mean? All in your target language. You're using it as a tool,
cues.zh: 在这门新语言中，你会说：这个怎么说？我不明白。请再说一遍。这是什么意思？全都用你的目标语言来说。你把它当作工具，

cues.en: making it useful to you. It's relevant to learn other things about the language. By week two, you should be saying things like me, this, you, that, give,
cues.zh: 让它为你所用。学习这门语言的其他内容也很重要。到了第二周，你应该能说出“我”“这个”“你”“那个”“给”之类的词，

cues.en: you know, hot, simple pronouns, simple nouns,
cues.zh: 还有“你知道”“热”，以及简单的代词、简单的名词，

cues.en: Simple verbs. Simple adjectives. Communicating like a baby. And by the third or fourth week, you're getting into what I call glue words.
cues.zh: 简单的动词，简单的形容词。像婴儿一样交流。到了第三或第四周，你就会开始接触我所说的连接词。

cues.en: Although, but, therefore, these are logical
cues.zh: 比如“虽然”“但是”“因此”，这些都是逻辑上的

cues.en: transformers that tie bits of a language together,
cues.zh: Transformer，把语言中的各个片段连接起来，

cues.en: allowing you to make more complex meaning.
cues.zh: 让你能够表达更复杂的含义。

cues.en: At that point, you're talking.
cues.zh: 到了这个阶段，你就开始说话了。

cues.en: And when you're doing that, you should get yourself a language parent.
cues.zh: 当你做到这一点时，你应该找一位语言家长。

cues.en: If you look at how children and parents interact, understand what this means.
cues.zh: 看看孩子和父母是如何互动的，你就能明白这是什么意思。

cues.en: When a child is speaking, it'll be using simple words, simple combinations,
cues.zh: 孩子说话时，会使用简单的词语和简单的组合，

cues.en: sometimes quite strange,
cues.zh: 有时听起来相当奇怪，

cues.en: sometimes very strange pronunciation.
cues.zh: 有时发音会非常奇怪。

cues.en: Other people from outside the family don't understand it.
cues.zh: 家人以外的其他人听不懂。

cues.en: But the parents do.
cues.zh: 但父母听得懂。

cues.en: And so, the kid has a safe environment,
cues.zh: 所以，孩子拥有一个安全的环境，

cues.en: gets confidence.
cues.zh: 也会获得自信。

cues.en: The parents talk to the children with body language and with simple language they know the child understands.
cues.zh: 父母会用肢体语言，以及孩子能理解的简单语言和孩子交流。

cues.en: So you have a comprehensible input environment that's safe, We know it works, otherwise none of you would speak your mother tongue.
cues.zh: 所以你有一个安全且可理解输入的环境。我们知道这有效，否则你们没人会说母语。

cues.en: So you get yourself a language parent who's somebody interested in you as a person, who will communicate with you essentially as an equal, but pay attention to help you understand the message.
cues.zh: 所以你要找一个语言家长，一个对你这个人感兴趣的人，他会基本以平等的方式和你交流，但会注意帮你理解信息。

cues.en: There are four rules of a language parent. Spouses, by the way, are not very good at this. Okay? But the four rules are, first of all, they will work hard to understand what you mean even when you're way off bib.
cues.zh: 语言家长有四条规则。顺便说，配偶不太擅长这个。好吧？四条规则是：首先，即使你错得离谱，他们也会努力理解你的意思。

cues.en: Secondly,
cues.zh: 第二，

cues.en: they will never correct your mistakes.
cues.zh: 他们从不纠正你的错误。

cues.en: Thirdly, they will feedback their understanding of what you're saying so that you can respond
cues.zh: 第三，他们会反馈他们对你说的话的理解，这样你可以回应

cues.en: appropriately and get that feedback, and then they will use words that you know.
cues.zh: 恰当地回应并得到那个反馈，然后他们会用你认识的词。

cues.en: The sixth thing you have to do
cues.zh: 第六件事你必须做

cues.en: is copy the face. You've got to get the muscles working right so you can sound in a way that people will understand you.
cues.zh: 是模仿面部。你得让肌肉正确运作，这样你说出来的话人们才能听懂。

cues.en: There's a couple of things you do. One is you you need to hear how it feels and feel how it sounds, which means you have a feedback loop operating in your face. But ideally, if you can look at a native speaker and just observe how they use their face, let your unconscious mind absorb the rules,
cues.zh: 有几件事要做。一是你需要听到它感觉如何，感受它听起来怎样，这意味着你脸上有一个反馈回路在运作。但理想情况下，如果你能看着母语者，观察他们如何使用面部，让你的潜意识吸收规则，

cues.en: then you're going to be able to pick it up. And if you can't get a native speaker to look at, you can use stuff like this.
cues.zh: 然后你就能学会它。如果你找不到母语者来看，你可以用这样的东西。

cues.en: Sing.
cues.zh: 唱

cues.en: Song.
cues.zh: 歌曲

cues.en: King.
cues.zh: 国王

cues.en: Song.
cues.zh: 歌曲

cues.en: Hung.
cues.zh: 悬挂

cues.en: And the final idea here, the final action you need to take is something that I call direct connect.
cues.zh: 这里最后一个理念，也是你需要采取的最后一个行动，我称之为直接连接。

cues.en: What does this mean? Well, most people learning a second language sort of take the mother tongue words and their target words and go over them again and again in their mind to try and remember them. Really inefficient.
cues.zh: 这是什么意思？大多数人在学习第二语言时，都会把母语词和目标语言的词放在脑中反复对照，试图记住它们。效率非常低。

cues.en: What you need to do is realize that everything you know is an image inside your mind, its feelings. If you talk about fire, you can smell the smoke, you can hear the crackling,
cues.zh: 你需要意识到，你所知道的一切，都是脑海中的一种影像，也包含相应的感受。比如说到火，你能闻到烟味，听到噼啪声，

cues.en: you can see the flames. So what you do is you go into that imagery and all of that memory and you come out with another pathway. So I just call it one same box, different path.
cues.zh: 也能看到火焰。所以，你要进入这些影像和记忆，从中找到另一条路径。我把它称为：同一个盒子，不同的路径。

cues.en: You come out that pathway and you build it over time. You become more and more skilled and just connecting the new sounds to those images that you already have, into that internal representation.
cues.zh: 你要沿着这条路径走出来，并随着时间不断构建它。你会越来越擅长把新的声音连接到已有的影像上，连接到你的内部表征中。

cues.en: And over time, you even become naturally good at that process that becomes unconscious.
cues.zh: 随着时间推移，你甚至会自然而然地掌握这个过程，让它变成无意识的行为。

cues.en: So there are five principles that you need to work with.
cues.zh: 所以，你需要遵循五项原则。

cues.en: Seven actions.
cues.zh: 七个行动。

cues.en: If you do any of them,
cues.zh: 只要你做其中任何一项，

cues.en: you're going to improve and remember these are things under your control as the learner.
cues.zh: 你都会有所提高。记住，这些都是作为学习者的你能够控制的事情。

cues.en: Do them all. You're going to be fluent in the second language in six months. Thank you.
cues.zh: 全部做到。六个月内，你就能流利地使用第二语言。谢谢。
